Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# ARC outline-grid inference

When demos show 1-valued orthogonal outline shapes transformed with colors 2 and 3:

1. Infer the actual operation directly from each demonstration. Do not assume all connected components are independent; check whether shapes are grouped or their bounding frames overlap.
2. Compare outputs cell-by-cell against inputs. Identify precisely which zeros become color 2 (often an added external frame) and color 3 (often interior fill), and note preserved zeros or intentional holes.

5. Validate frame geometry against examples: thickness, whether corners are included, whether frames are clipped at the grid edge, and whether two adjacent frames merge/overlap.
6. Keep the original dimensions. Before submission, mechanically verify that the output is rectangular, has the same expected size if demos indicate that, and every cell is an integer 0–9. Avoid hand-copying scripts' long outputs without row-length checks.
7. In uncertain cases, request demos until the cap, then derive candidate transformations and test them on every demo before applying to test input. Incorrect attempts provide no corrective signal beyond count, so do not repeatedly submit minor variants without a clear hypothesis.
